title: Frontend: Implement LRUCache
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Implement LRUCache. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({capacity,commands}) for an LRU cache. put{key,value} returns null; get{key} returns cached JSON value or null and promotes recency. Updating a key promotes it. capacity is a nonnegative integer. Return outputs; capacity=0 stores nothing.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Combine a key-to-node map with a doubly linked list, moving accessed/updated nodes to the most-recent end and evicting the least-recent node at capacity.
alternativeApproaches: Add TTL expiration and explain why recency, expiration, and capacity are independent policies.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Read promotes key; overwrite promotes key; eviction.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
